script_nghe: Good morning. Today we’re looking at urban waste. The average city dweller in this region produces around four hundred and eighty kilograms of waste a year. Of that, only about twenty-three per cent is currently recycled — the official figure of thirty per cent includes material used as road fill, which I’d argue shouldn’t count. The single biggest problem is food waste in apartment buildings, where separate collection is rare. The new policy sets a target for twenty thirty-five. My own view is that the first step should be to charge for collection by weight — it’s unpopular but it works. Next week we’ll be looking at water treatment.

> **The recycling paradox**
> 
> Recycling rates in wealthy countries rose steadily for three decades, and the public came to regard the practice as an environmental success. Since around 2018, however, several countries have reported falling rates, and some have quietly increased the proportion of waste sent to incinerators.
> 
> Part of the explanation lies overseas. For years, much of the material collected in Europe and North America was exported to Asia for processing. In 2018, China stopped accepting most foreign plastic waste, citing contamination levels. Other countries absorbed some of the flow but soon introduced similar restrictions. Material that had been counted as recycled was suddenly without a destination.
> 
> The deeper problem is economic. Recycled plastic competes with new plastic made from oil, and when oil prices fall, recycled material becomes uncompetitive. Collection continues because councils are obliged to provide it, but the collected material may be stored, burned or landfilled.
> 
> Some analysts argue that the focus on recycling has itself been harmful, because it directed attention away from reducing consumption. Producing a plastic bottle and then recycling it uses far more energy than not producing it. A smaller number go further, suggesting that recycling campaigns were promoted by the packaging industry precisely because they placed responsibility on consumers rather than manufacturers.

**True / False / Not Given (7–10):**
7. Recycling rates in wealthy countries have risen continuously since 2018.
8. China’s decision in 2018 was based on contamination of the waste.
9. Recycled plastic becomes less competitive when oil prices fall.
10. Most analysts believe recycling campaigns were created by the packaging industry.

**Hoàn thành câu (11–14):**
11. Some countries have increased waste sent to ____________.
12. After China’s ban, other countries introduced similar ____________.
13. Councils continue collection because they are ____________ to.
14. Critics say the focus on recycling drew attention away from reducing ____________.

writing.de_tom_tat: Task 1, ≥150 từ, 20 phút: mô tả biểu đồ đường về lượng khí thải carbon của 3 quốc gia trong 30 năm.
writing.bai_mau:
The line graph compares carbon emissions in three countries over a thirty-year period from 1990 to 2020, measured in millions of tonnes.

Overall, emissions rose considerably in Country A and Country B, whereas those in Country C declined steadily. By the end of the period, Country A had become by far the largest emitter.

In 1990, Country C produced the highest level of emissions, at approximately 600 million tonnes, while Country A stood at only 250 million. Country A then experienced sustained growth, rising sharply after 2000 and reaching a peak of around 900 million tonnes in 2015, before levelling off in the final five years.

Country B followed a similar though less dramatic pattern, climbing gradually from 300 to roughly 550 million tonnes, with a brief dip in 2008. Country C, by contrast, fell consistently throughout the period, dropping to just under 400 million tonnes by 2020 — a reduction of approximately one third.

The most striking feature is the reversal of positions: the country with the highest emissions in 1990 had the lowest by 2020.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Có đủ 4 phần bắt buộc: paraphrase đề · đoạn Overview · hai đoạn số liệu chi tiết. Nêu đủ mốc đầu, đỉnh, cuối cho cả ba đường. Không đưa ý kiến cá nhân — đúng yêu cầu Task 1.
Đoạn Overview đặt ngay sau mở bài (bắt buộc). So sánh bằng whereas · while · by contrast · though less dramatic. Câu cuối nêu đặc điểm nổi bật nhất.

Động từ xu hướng đa dạng: rose · declined · experienced growth · reaching a peak · levelling off · climbing · dip · fell · dropping. Trạng từ: considerably · steadily · sharply · gradually · consistently.
Quá khứ hoàn thành (had become) · mệnh đề rút gọn (rising sharply, before levelling off) · bị động (measured in millions) · so sánh nhất (by far the largest).

dang_hoc: Task 1 bắt buộc có đoạn Overview ngay sau mở bài. Thiếu nó là trần band 5 cho Task Achievement.
Overview nêu xu hướng chung, không nêu số cụ thể. Số liệu để dành cho các đoạn sau.
TUYỆT ĐỐI không đưa ý kiến, nguyên nhân, hay giải pháp vào Task 1. Chỉ mô tả những gì thấy.
Bộ động từ+trạng từ cần thuộc: rise/fall + sharply/gradually/steadily/slightly · peak at · level off · fluctuate.
loi_thuong_gap: ❌ Không có đoạn Overview → mất điểm nặng nhất của Task 1.
❌ Liệt kê mọi con số mà không so sánh → Task 1 là bài so sánh, không phải bảng số.
❌ Viết "I think emissions rose because…" → Task 1 không được suy đoán nguyên nhân.
❌ Dùng hiện tại đơn cho dữ liệu quá khứ → biểu đồ có mốc năm cụ thể thì dùng quá khứ.

speaking.de_tom_tat: Part 1 — Environment: Do you worry about pollution? / What do you do to help? / Is your city clean?

cau_tra_loi.mau: I do, particularly air quality. On bad days you can actually see the haze over the city, and I notice it when I cycle.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Chi tiết cụ thể từ trải nghiệm ("see the haze", "when I cycle") làm câu trả lời sống động.

cau_tra_loi.hoi: What do you do to help?
cau_tra_loi.mau: Small things, mostly. I've cut down on single-use plastic and I cycle rather than drive when I can. I'm aware that's fairly limited, though.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "I'm aware that's fairly limited" — tự nhận xét, thể hiện tư duy phản biện. Rất được điểm ở Part 3.

cau_tra_loi.mau: Cleaner than it was, but there's a long way to go. Waste collection has improved noticeably, though recycling is still almost non-existent.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: So sánh với quá khứ + nêu mặt còn thiếu — cấu trúc trả lời cân bằng.

cham_diem.vi_sao: Trả lời có sắc thái và tự nhận xét.
haze · single-use plastic · waste collection · non-existent.
Cleaner than it was · has improved · I'm aware that…

meo_noi: "Cleaner than it was, but there's a long way to go" — mẫu câu so sánh hiện tại với quá khứ, dùng được cho rất nhiều chủ đề.
Tự nhận xét về câu trả lời của mình ("that's fairly limited") là dấu hiệu tư duy phản biện.
